title: Performance Modeling and Analysis of a de Bruijn Graph Based Local Assembly Kernel on Multiple Vendor GPUs
problem: Implementing an efficient de Bruijn graph-based local assembly kernel that maintains performance and portability across NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs while handling integer-only operations, irregular memory patterns, and non-deterministic bioinformatics workloads that differ fundamentally from traditional HPC and AI workloads.
motivation: Local assembly is a critical step in large-scale genome assembly pipelines, and achieving efficient multi-GPU portability enables broad accessibility of bioinformatics applications across different hardware vendors.
method: The authors write GPU code that assembles genome sequences by constructing de Bruijn graphs—networks where overlapping DNA fragments connect together—and use hash tables (fast lookup structures) to efficiently store sequence data. They evaluate this code across NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs, identifying performance bottlenecks and hardware-specific differences. By analyzing these results, they uncover that existing GPU performance prediction tools don't accurately model integer-heavy bioinformatics workloads and propose specific improvements.
key_novelty: Existing GPU performance prediction tools fail to accurately model integer-heavy bioinformatics workloads, as revealed by cross-vendor testing.
contributions: Cross-vendor GPU evaluation of de Bruijn graph-based local assembly kernel on NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel architectures
Identification of performance bottlenecks specific to integer-heavy bioinformatics workloads
Proposed modifications to existing performance modeling and analysis tools for bioinformatics application kernels
Analysis of hardware-specific optimizations and their impact on portability trade-offs

metrics.speedup: kernel performance across GPU vendors (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel)

limitations: Limitations and constraints are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: multi-vendor GPU performance portability for bioinformatics kernels
